definition_quote.value: the examining, diagnosing, and treating of any visual defect or abnormal condition of the human eye or its appendages within the scope established in this article or associated rules and the performance of those procedures taught and trained through schools or colleges of optometry accredited by the Accreditation Council on Optometric Education, or its successors or equivalents

methods_authorized.quote: Examine, diagnose, and treat diseases and conditions of the human eye and its appendages within the scope established in this article or associated rules

drug_authority.value: A certificate holder may administer or prescribe topical pharmaceutical agents for the anterior segment; prescribe oral drugs from the board-established formulary (Schedules III, IV, V, plus oral antibiotics, NSAIDs, and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors); prescribe and dispense pharmaceutical-delivering contact lenses; administer epinephrine by injection for anaphylaxis; and, with additional certification, administer other injectable pharmaceutical agents. Schedule II controlled substances are prohibited except hydrocodone/hydrocodone-containing drugs may be prescribed for no more than three days by an oral pharmaceutical certified licensee.
